currentContext.expansion: CBPL is asset-light and owns no manufacturing plant - its approved formulations are made by third-party contract manufacturers on loan-licence or principal-to-principal basis - so the expansion narrative is about securing dedicated capacity rather than building it on its own balance sheet. Management's stated plan is to enter a long-term MOU and identify a dedicated, high-tech fully automated state-of-the-art manufacturing facility near Mumbai and Ahmedabad for vaccination, injections and other dosage forms, approved by FDA and WHO/GMP, with an intent to upgrade it up to PIC/S and MHRA standards. Alongside that, management plans to create a contract manufacturing and development FDF (Finished Dosage Formulations) vertical offering a single-point solution from raw materials to compression to bulk packing, and a CRAMS (Contract Research and Manufacturing Services) vertical for end-to-end formulation development and commercial manufacturing. On the distribution side it plans to set up warehousing and distribution centres at additional locations to serve the Indian market, and a new warehousing and distribution facility for the Pharma and API-Chemical business offering bulk repacking for retail customers with customised requirements. The product-side expansion is a phased vaccines launch - Hepatitis A and Inactivated Polio Vaccine in the first phase, with Pneumococcal and Varicella vaccines to follow phase-wise within 3-4 years - plus new launches in chronic disease and anti-allergic ranges, expansion of the secondary sales team and field force, deeper state-wise penetration, and investment in R&D for formulations. No commissioning date, capex quantum or capacity figure is disclosed for any of these; the accounts state that as per management's best estimate there is no capital commitment as on the date of the financial statement, and no dividend was recommended so that profit could be retained for the future expansion of the Company.
